<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.20</span> Partitions of unity, paracompactness and second countability (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html#subsection_Integral_Whole_Manifold" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_Integral_Whole_Manifold">8.2.1</a>)</h1></header>
<p>The integral (<a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html#eq_integral_manifold" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_manifold">8.4</a>) needs a partition of unity subordinate to the cover of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> by the chart domains of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{A}^\uparrow\)</span> (Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html#subsection_Integral_Whole_Manifold" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_Integral_Whole_Manifold">8.2.1</a>). This appendix shows that partitions of unity subordinate to every open cover exist because <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> is Hausdorff and second countable (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Topological_Manifolds">3</a>), that the property they actually rest on is paracompactness, and that neither condition can be dropped. Compactness and closures are as in Appendix <a class="dg-xref" href="support-integrals.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_appendix_support_integrals">B.19</a>.</p>
<ul class="dg-itemize dg-depth-1">
<li><p><strong>Paracompactness.</strong> A <strong>refinement</strong> of an open cover <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\)</span> is an open cover <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{W}_b \}\)</span> with every  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{W}_b\)</span> contained in some <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_a\)</span>. A space is <strong>paracompact</strong> if every open cover has a locally finite refinement:  finitely many sets near each point, instead of finitely many sets altogether as for compactness. This is the property  partitions of unity rest on. On the one hand, a partition of unity <span class="math inline">\(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \}\)</span> subordinate to <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\)</span> contains  one: the open sets <span class="math inline">\(\{ \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n &gt; 0 \}\)</span> cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, since <span class="math inline">\(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = 1\)</span>, each lies in  <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_a\)</span>, and they are locally finite, as the supports are. Partitions of unity  subordinate to every open cover thus exist only on paracompact spaces. On the other hand, they are built on a locally  finite refinement, as below, where Hausdorff and second countability are what produce it.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Existence.</strong> Let <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\)</span> be an open cover of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>Exhaustion by compact sets (second countability).</em> Every point has an open neighbourhood with compact  closure: the preimage, in a chart, of a small open ball, whose closure lies in the preimage of the closed ball,  compact, and closed since <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> is Hausdorff. The elements of a countable basis of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}\)</span> contained in such  neighbourhoods still cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span> and have compact closures: call them <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{B}_1, \mathcal{B}_2, \dots\)</span>. Set  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_1 \coloneqq \overline{\mathcal{B}_1}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_{j+1} \coloneqq \overline{\mathcal{B}_1} \cup \dots \cup \overline{\mathcal{B}_{m_j}}\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(m_j &gt; j\)</span> so  large that <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{B}_1, \dots, \mathcal{B}_{m_j}\)</span> cover the compact <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_j\)</span>. Then every <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_j\)</span> is compact,  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_j \subseteq \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_{j+1}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\bigcup_j \mathcal{K}_j = \mathcal{M}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Compact rings.</em> With <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{K}_0 = \mathcal{K}_{-1} \coloneqq \emptyset\)</span>, the compact sets  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{R}_j \coloneqq \mathcal{K}_{j+1} \setminus \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_j\)</span> cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>, and each lies in the open set  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_j \coloneqq \operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_{j+2} \setminus \mathcal{K}_{j-1}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Finitely many bump functions per ring (compactness).</em> For each <span class="math inline">\(p \in \mathcal{R}_j\)</span>, take a bump function  <span class="math inline">\(\varphi_p \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\varphi_p \geq 0\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\varphi_p(p) &gt; 0\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \varphi_p\)</span> compact and contained in  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_j \cap \mathcal{U}_a\)</span> for some <span class="math inline">\(a\)</span> (Section <a class="dg-xref" href="../tangent-spaces/cotangent-space.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Cotangent_Space">4.2</a>; its extension by zero outside a chart  domain uses again that compact sets are closed). The open sets <span class="math inline">\(\{ \varphi_p &gt; 0 \}\)</span> cover the compact <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{R}_j\)</span>, so  finitely many suffice. Over all <span class="math inline">\(j\)</span>, this gives countably many <span class="math inline">\(\varphi_1, \varphi_2, \dots\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Local finiteness (paracompactness).</em> Every point lies in some <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{int} \mathcal{K}_m\)</span>, which is disjoint  from <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}_j\)</span> for <span class="math inline">\(j &gt; m\)</span>, so it meets only the supports chosen for <span class="math inline">\(j \leq m\)</span>: finitely many. The sets  <span class="math inline">\(\{ \varphi_n &gt; 0 \}\)</span> thus form a countable locally finite refinement of <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Normalize.</em> Near each point, <span class="math inline">\(\sum_k \varphi_k\)</span> is a finite sum of smooth functions, hence smooth, and it is  positive everywhere, since the sets <span class="math inline">\(\{ \varphi_k &gt; 0 \}\)</span> cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>. Hence  <span class="math display">\[
            \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \coloneqq \frac{\varphi_n}{\sum_k \varphi_k}
        \]</span>  is a partition of unity subordinate to <span class="math inline">\(\{ \mathcal{U}_a \}\)</span>: <span class="math inline">\(0 \leq \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n \leq 1\)</span>,  <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = \operatorname{supp} \varphi_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_a\)</span>, locally finite by step 4, and <span class="math inline">\(\sum_n \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n = 1\)</span>.  <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p></li>
</ol>
<p>Second countability enters in step 1, and only there: it supplies countably many sets, hence an exhaustion by  countably many compact sets. Hausdorff enters in steps 1 and 3, by making compact sets closed. Compactness then  reduces each ring to finitely many bump functions, and the rings, each meeting only its neighbours, make the whole  family locally finite.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Hausdorff cannot be dropped.</strong> On the line with two origins (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Topological_Manifolds">3</a>), take  the cover by its two copies of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_A \ni 0_A\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_B \ni 0_B\)</span>, and group the functions of a subordinate  partition of unity into <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_B\)</span>, with supports in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_A\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}_B\)</span>. Since <span class="math inline">\(0_A \notin \mathcal{U}_B\)</span>,  <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_B = 0\)</span> near <span class="math inline">\(0_A\)</span>, so <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A = 1\)</span> near <span class="math inline">\(0_A\)</span>, i.e. at all <span class="math inline">\(t \neq 0\)</span> close to <span class="math inline">\(0\)</span>. Every neighbourhood of <span class="math inline">\(0_B\)</span>  contains such <span class="math inline">\(t\)</span>, so <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A(0_B) = 1\)</span> by continuity, contradicting <span class="math inline">\(0_B \notin \operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_A\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><strong>Second countability cannot be dropped.</strong> A countable partition of unity subordinate to the cover by chart  domains, as used in (<a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html#eq_integral_manifold" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_manifold">8.4</a>), forces it. Every point has some <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n &gt; 0\)</span>, so  <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M} = \bigcup_n \operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\)</span>, and each <span class="math inline">\(\operatorname{supp} \textrm{\runic ᚹ}_n\)</span> lies in a chart domain: countably many charts  <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}_k, \mathscr{X}_k)\)</span> cover <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{M}\)</span>. The preimages <span class="math inline">\(\mathscr{X}_k^{-1}\big( B \cap \mathscr{X}_k(\mathcal{U}_k) \big)\)</span> of the open balls <span class="math inline">\(B\)</span>  with rational centres and radii then form a countable basis of <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{O}\)</span>. The long line of  Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../topological-manifolds/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Topological_Manifolds">3</a>, which is connected and cannot be covered by countably many charts, therefore  admits no such partition of unity<sup class="dg-fnref"><a href="#fn-4" id="fnref-4" role="doc-noteref" aria-label="Footnote 4">4</a></sup>, and integrals over it cannot be built from chart integrals as in (<a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html#eq_integral_manifold" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_integral_manifold">8.4</a>).</p></li>
</ul>
<section class="dg-footnotes" role="doc-endnotes"><div class="dg-fn" id="fn-4" role="doc-footnote"><a class="dg-fn-num" href="#fnref-4" aria-label="Back to the text">4</a><div class="dg-fn-body"><p>Countability matters only for manifolds with uncountably many connected components, e.g. uncountably many disjoint  copies of <span class="math inline">\(\mathbb{R}\)</span>: they are paracompact and admit partitions of unity, necessarily with uncountably many functions,  and are not second countable.</p></div></div></section>
